facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: jñātidāsī yato jātā kaikeyī tu sahoshitā, prāsādaṃ cāru saṃprāpya dṛṣṭavaty ayodhikām
facts.text: In the Valmiki Ramayana, Manthara is described as an elderly, hunchbacked royal maidservant who accompanied Queen Kaikeyi from the northwestern kingdom of Kekeya.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: tau yācasva varau rājānaṃ dehi me varau, rāmasya pravrājanaṃ caiva bharatasya abhiṣecanam
facts.text: Manthara poisoned Kaikeyi's mind by reminding her of two outstanding boons previously granted by King Dasharatha during the ancient celestial war against the demon Timidhvaja.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi rāme pravrājite vanam, prajānāṃ hṛdaye rājā sthiraṃ sthāpayiṣyati
facts.text: Manthara specifically calculated that Rama must be exiled to the forest for 14 years to ensure that Bharata could firmly entrench his royal power across the kingdom.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: नामु मंथरा मंदमति चेरी कैकेइ केरि। अजस पेटारी ताहि करि गई गिरा मति फेरि।।
facts.text: In the Awadhi epic Ramcharitmanas, the celestials plead with Saraswati, the goddess of speech, to alter Manthara's intellect so that Rama's exile and Ravana's eventual destruction could unfold.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Dundubhi hearing these words of the Grandsire was born in the world of men as the hunchbacked Manthara to accomplish that celestial purpose.
facts.text: In the Mahabharata's Ramopakhyana, sage Markandeya states that Brahma commanded a Gandharva named Dundubhi to be born in the human world as Manthara to create obstacles for Rama.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pramadāḥ kṣamyatām iti, hatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tu kaikeyīṃ rāmo naiva vadiṣyati
facts.text: When Shatrughna violently dragged Manthara to kill her after Dasharatha's death, Prince Bharata restrained him on the grounds that slaying a woman violates dharma.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: In 1975, a joint project of the ASI and the Indian Institute of Advanced Study on the 'Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites' was initiated, headed by B.B. Lal.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India collaborated on the Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites project initiated in 1975 under former Director General B. B. Lal to examine the antiquity of key locations mentioned in the epic.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: This volume deals with a 250-metre long brick tank which is a unique example of Indian hydraulic engineering 2000 years ago.
facts.text: Excavations at Sringaverapura conducted between 1977 and 1986 by the Archaeological Survey of India uncovered a sophisticated brick hydraulic tank complex measuring over 250 metres in length.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: This excavation confirmed that Ayodhya was first occupied in the 7th century BCE with Northern Black Polished Ware.
facts.text: Excavation trenches in Ayodhya by the Archaeological Survey of India established initial human settlement levels associated with Northern Black Polished Ware dating back to around 700 BCE.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The lowest cultural period of the site yields Northern Black Polished Ware from circa the early first millennium BCE, contrasting sharply with traditional Treta Yuga chronology.
facts.text: Archaeological datings of the primary Ramayana sites place early urbanization between 1300 and 700 BCE, which conflicts with traditional astronomical calculations that date the events millennia earlier.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: A popular folklore motif explains Manthara's hostility through a childhood incident where Rama struck her hump with a toy bow and mud balls.
facts.text: Popular Indian folk legends and traditional oral kathas assert that young Rama once mockingly shot mud pellets at Manthara's hunched back, creating a lingering personal grudge that motivated her vengeance.
